title: fix: UI deadcode check rejects diagnostics fixture types
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the UI findings in the scheduled dependency check caused by two diagnostics types exported only for tests.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39062485709/job/117483329820

## User Impact

No user-visible or runtime behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the unused `CommandLaneSnapshot` re-export and `CommandLaneDynamicSummary` alias. Debug-page fixtures now derive their lane and nullable dynamic types from the existing production `CommandLaneDiagnostics` contract, so the tests retain the same type checks without expanding the production API.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Debug-page test file | 17 tests passed |
| UI typecheck | Passed |
| Independent P2 review | No actionable findings |
| Scoped lint and formatting | Passed |
| Production Knip | Both UI findings removed; 10 core exports and 1 root dependency still fail exactly as in the supplied scheduled run |

Two files, 5 lines added and 11 removed. Diagnostics module: 52 → 49 lines; test: 701 → 698 lines. No runtime or visual change, so no build or screenshots are needed.

The remaining production Knip findings are outside this UI repair: the root `@modelcontextprotocol/client` dependency, `createHeartbeatResponseTool`, `runScopedSqliteReadOnlyOperation`, seven diagnostic reset exports, and `decodeOpenClawStateReadReply`. No ignores were added.
